The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production – the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6511a2f8-e8e4-11f1-b921-81da3ab2acbb/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261125-160230-160715-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6511a2f8-e8e4-11f1-b921-81da3ab2acbb/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261125-160230-160715-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6b2b99a0-e8e4-11f1-98e9-cb2d864e59f7</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:21:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261125-iranian-family-seeks-release-of-twin-sisters-facing-death-penalty-and-25-years-in-prison</link><description>

US officials say the material, which was once used as a detonator in munitions, had become unstable and was at risk at risk of spontaneous explosion. But the risk of a toxic cloud of lead dust spreading out from the blast zone has caused public safety fears among locals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/16b2359e-e8eb-11f1-8c75-95e072ff0a91/w:1024/p:16x9/Iowa-thumbnail.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/16b2359e-e8eb-11f1-8c75-95e072ff0a91/w:1024/p:16x9/Iowa-thumbnail.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9198524e-e8ea-11f1-b047-a5e56909f287</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:14:40 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Colombia: Security forces rescue hostages in supermarket siege</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261125-colombia-security-forces-rescue-hostages-in-supermarket-siege</link><description>

'Irresponsible' to compare it to Chernobyl, agency chief says ]]> NASA has sent three different research aircraft and is using a satellite-based instrument to support the U.S. Army's detonation of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, the agency announced yesterday (Nov. 24).

After a week-long delay caused by public concern over the event creating clouds of lead and toxic materials, today (Nov. 25) around 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT) the U.S. Army has planned to execute a controlled detonation of five tons of aging explosives at the ammunition plant. The detonation follows concerns that cooling winter temperatures or attempts to chemically neutralize the materials could lead to an unexpected, uncontrolled explosion.

"In challenging circumstances such as this, you want the nation's best on the field. That is precisely why you call on NASA, putting our airborne and space-based sensors and some of the brightest scientific minds in the country to work," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in an online statement.

To support this detonation, NASA deployed three research aircraft: a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III from NASA's Langley Research Center and a B200 from NASA Ames. The agency is also monitoring the situation using its TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) instrument which is mounted and orbiting Earth on a commercial satellite.

"Working alongside our partners across the federal government, NASA is utilizing its advanced scientific instruments and expertise to collect environmental and atmospheric data to inform the broader federal response," NASA stated.

The environmental monitoring using TEMPO is especially important as the materials to be detonated include lead azide and other toxic components that are causing not just environmental worries, but significant local concern over possible health repercussions. This concern is severe enough that, following detonation, officials are encouraging local residents to stay indoors with the doors and windows closed for 24-28 hours.

In fact, the CDC has activated an emergency response "to provide accurate public health communication and technical assistance," the CDC stated online. They have also offered additional guidance for locals to try and mitigate as much exposure to toxic materials like lead dust as possible.

In the map below, which comes from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers using satellite data, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency.

While this planned detonation has unsurprisingly caused concern among locals and nationwide, Isaacman has urged the public not to mischaracterize the event as something larger.

"Even if it's hyperbole, it is irresponsible to characterize this as a 'Chernobyl event,'" he said online in response to someone likening the event to the infamous nuclear accident.

"When there is no reactor and there are no fission products. This is a controlled detonation of aging explosive material and is being handled in the most responsible way possible."

]]> <![CDATA[ Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026 ]]>

Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches.

What is it?

On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak.

When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11.

The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind.

And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches.

Why is it incredible?

On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption.

This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case.

But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023. And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land.

"I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement. "But we'll have to wait and see."

]]> <![CDATA[ Watch live: Europe unveils 1st close-up views of asteroid Dimorphos after NASA's DART impact ]]> After a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25).

The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024. Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos, a "rubble pile" asteroid, and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test, which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid.

Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25). Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency.

At Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth.

The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids.

Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects.

"ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement. "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact?

"Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test."

ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse.

Hera even stopped by Mars on its way to the asteroids, snapping pictures of its moon Deimos.

Hera will remain at the Didymos-Dimorphos system for months, deploying cubesats that will study the asteroids with visible and infrared light cameras and radar instruments.

Through Hera, scientists hope to refine planetary defense techniques so that, should the time ever come, humanity has options for defending itself against incoming space rocks like the one that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

"Through many years of hard work our international collaboration managed to do just that, and for the very highest of intentions: to help make Earth safer," said Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli.

It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole.

That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused.

That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth.

Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter, the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Hence Euclid's nickname as the "dark universe detective."

This research, along with Euclid's discovery of at least 12 that date back around 13 billion years, shows that this pioneering space telescope launched in 2023 could also make a major contribution to our understanding of black holes and their growth.

On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.

Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere.

After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets, the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched.

Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space. (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control.

Why it mattered

Billed as the "most successful sounding rocket of the space age," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so.

"The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview. "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds."

While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper.

New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.

NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas."

Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity.

As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf, the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived "red giant" phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris.

During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space.

To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming.

"Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action."

The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life.

The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower rate. This mass loss then increased sharply over the following 1,000 years. This led to the creation of a lumpy shell of gas now seen as a tangle of material filaments around the dying star. The fact that these filaments have a spiral shape could indicate that IRAS 06530-0213 has an unseen partner orbiting it, stirring the gas.

Meanwhile, the hourglass-shaped nebula immediately around the star began to take shape around 700 years ago, meaning that the red giant phase for IRAS 06530-0213 only ended very recently, in cosmic terms at least.

There are also unexpected elements to the ALMA observations of IRAS 06530-0213.

Strange chemistry of dying star

The team discovered an unexpected abundance of heavy versions, or isotopes, of elements like carbon, oxygen and nitrogen around IRAS 06530-0213.

This doesn't conform to models of how stars like IRAS 06530-0213 forge elements and mix them into their surroundings, though similar signatures have been seen around odd stellar objects, with violent bursts of nuclear fusion thought to be the cause.

As well as seeing something unexpected, the researchers didn't detect something they expected to observe.

Dying stars like IRAS 06530-0213 have previously been known to have companions, typically sitting with them inside compact disks of dust. These disks are indirect evidence of material being dragged from the close companion star to the dying star. This is a process scientists have used to explain jet-sculpted hourglass shapes.

However, ALMA failed to detect such disk around IRAS 06530. The team suggests that this could be because a disk existed, albeit briefly, during which time it powered a short burst of high-speed jets that helped sculpt the hourglass, following this the disk simply faded away.

"Dying stars so often have hidden companions that reshape their ejected material into intricate, bipolar or multipolar forms instead of simple spheres," Sahai concluded. "IRAS 06530 shows that the story is more complicated than the tidy explanation we've been using."

The team's research was published on Friday (Nov. 20) in The Astrophysical Journal.

   <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) i po sérii demonstrací a veřejné kritiky neslevuje ze svého postoje a programového prohlášení vlády a nechce ani slyšet o tom, že by vláda měla ustoupit ze záměru zrušit koncesionářské poplatky. Neoblomnost potvrdil pro Deník.cz v pořadu 15 minut Kateřiny Perknerové. Zopakoval, že vláda nechce Českou televizi a rozhlas kontrolovat, podle něj je cílem jen ulevit peněženkám občanů. Zasazuje se o to, aby média nezasáhly škrty, které by zapříčinily konec některých pořadů, například oblíbeného StarDance. Podle něj je to formát, který i kvůli svému charitativnímu přesahu do veřejnoprávních médií patří.</description>

   <description>Evropská unie schvaluje rozpočtový rámec na dalších sedm let. Objem peněz, se kterým bude hospodařit, se má snížit o 32 miliard eur.       <description>Spotřeba ovoce v posledních letech v Česku klesá. Padělané doklady sbírají policisté jako Pokémony</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906645-falesny-prukaz-kone-i-pas-antarktidy-padelane-doklady-sbiraji-policiste-jako-pokemony.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906645-falesny-prukaz-kone-i-pas-antarktidy-padelane-doklady-sbiraji-policiste-jako-pokemony.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Eva Hradilová</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Už deset let sbírají experti z Národního centra pro kontrolu dokladů dokumenty, které pocházejí z dílen padělatelů. Přestože se sraženému chodci omluvil, z místa události odjel, aniž by věc dále řešil.</description></item><item><title>Hitlerův oběd, oběšený farář i hlas Augustové. Nová roura odhalí tajemství Chrastavy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906637-hitleruv-obed-obeseny-farar-i-hlas-augustove-nova-roura-odhali-tajemstvi-chrastavy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906637-hitleruv-obed-obeseny-farar-i-hlas-augustove-nova-roura-odhali-tajemstvi-chrastavy.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V neděli 29. listopadu v 15 hodin se v Chrastavě slavnostně rozezvučí nový Poesiomat. Stand-up komik Lukáš Pavlásek včera nedorazil na své plánované vystoupení v Hejnicích na Liberecku, protože se nechal zlákat navigací a místo na sever Čech zamířil do stejnojmenné obce v Pardubickém kraji.</description></item><item><title>Před 10 lety zemřel v Liberci František Peterka, proslul jako Krakonoš z večerníčku</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906618-pred-10-lety-zemrel-v-liberci-frantisek-peterka-proslul-jako-krakonos-z-vecernicku.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906618-pred-10-lety-zemrel-v-liberci-frantisek-peterka-proslul-jako-krakonos-z-vecernicku.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Přesně před deseti lety, v pátek 25. listopadu 2016, zemřel známý herec František Peterka. Odešel ve věku čtyřiadevadesáti let, v libereckém Hospici sv. Zdislavy. Oblíbený představitel nejen pohádkového Krakonoše v Krkonošských pohádkách byl výraznou osobností Libereckého kraje.</description></item><item><title>Tygři vyhráli ve Varech 5:2. A utkání nakonec zvládli stejný výsledkem 5:2. Pytlík si v utkání připsal dvě branky a asistenci.</description></item><item><title>Útok na strážníka v Jablonci. Agresor ho napadl při zásahu u Kauflandu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906586-utok-na-straznika-v-jablonci-agresor-ho-napadl-pri-zasahu-u-kauflandu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906586-utok-na-straznika-v-jablonci-agresor-ho-napadl-pri-zasahu-u-kauflandu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 18:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Strážníci městské policie v Jablonci nad Nisou museli v pátek řešit nejen zraněného muže před prodejnou Kaufland, ale také agresivního kolemjdoucího, který hlídku slovně napadal, odmítal uposlechnout výzvy, a nakonec jednoho ze strážníků fyzicky napadl.</description></item><item><title>Policisté vypátrali ženu z Jablonce. ]]> Ezagutu Lužice aneb Poznejte Lužici https://www.vybezek.eu/297720-ezagutu-luzice-aneb-poznejte-luzici/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:23:04 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=297720 Literárně naučné miniturné po Čechách lužickosrbské spisovatelky Róži Domašcyny, básníka a překladatele Milana Hrabala a hudebníka Vojtěcha Kouby.

Ve dnech 3. a 4. listopadu 2026 proběhly dva večery věnované lužickosrbské literatuře a kultuře pod názvem Ezagutu Lužice (Poznejte Lužici), které pořádaly, ruku v ruce, nakladatelství Euskaldun a Společnost přátel Lužice. Nejednalo se o první takovou spolupráci, ale o vyvrcholení celého cyklu pořadů věnovaným menším jazykovým skupinám bez vlastní státnosti, které jsou nějakým způsobem svázány s českými zeměmi. První večer proběhl v Plzni v univerzitní kavárně Družba a následující den se přesunul takříkajíc na domácí hřiště do pražského Lužického semináře.

Hlavními hvězdami večerů byly Róža Domašcyna, jedna z nejvýznamnějších lužickosrbských autorek a Milan Hrabal, básník, překladatel, přítel a propagátor Lužice. O hudební doprovod se postaral Vojtěch Kouba, který představil publiku lužický folklór, ale zároveň i vlastní tvorbu.

Na první večer dorazilo asi čtyřicet zvídavých Plzeňanů, pro které bylo setkání s literaturou a historií nejmenšího západoslovanského národa iniciačním zážitkem. Milan Hrabal se ukázal, jako výborný průvodce lužicko-srbskými reáliemi i historií. Navíc bavil publikum tím, jak se postupně přiznával k různým překladatelským přehmatům. Poezie Róži Domašcyny a písně Vojtěcha Kouby vykouzlily čarovnou atmosféru jak v plzeňské studentské kavárně, tak pod barokní klenbou Lužického semináře.

Sychravé počasí za okny kontrastovalo s vřelou a neformální atmosférou obou večerů. U srdce zahřály i reakce návštěvníků. Etablovaný plzeňský básník Jan Sojka poklekl před organizátory večera na kolena, líbal jim ruce a děkoval za krásný večer. Herpetolog Ondřej Škach zase prohlásil, že nelituje toho, že vyměnil oslavu úspěšného odchovu zmije pavoučí v plzeňské ZOO, za lužickosrbský večer, neboť o zmijích ví všechno, ale o Lužici nevěděl doposud nic. Filolog Mikuláš Liptovský se nechal výkonem účinkujících dokonce strhnout ke slibu, že se na stará kolena pustí do studia sorabistiky. Studenty pražských uměleckých škol zase okouzlil Milan Hrabal natolik, že se zajímali o to, kdy bude mít v Lužickém semináři příští seminář o Lužici. Není divu, že se návštěvníci nechali vtáhnout do průběhu večera. Byl totiž úplně jiný, než obvykle literární večery bývají. Domašcyna s Hrabalem jsou na sebe mentálně navázaní a je na jejich vystoupení znát, že jsou sehraná dvojice. Kouba je pak skvěle doplňuje svými písněmi. Většina diváků slyšela asi poprvé dylanovku v lužické srbštině.  O pozitivních pocitech publika svědčí i ovace ve stoje, které následovaly po pražském večeru.

V době, kdy některé vlády vedou kulturní války proti vlastním občanům, tito se jim staví literaturou a radostí, kterou přináší umění slova. Je hezké vidět, když se lidé sejdou, aby vyslechli hlas malého národa a tím se o něco víc přiblížili ke břehům ostrova zapomenutých.

Martin Holý , Euskaldun
